advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] On TimeoutExpired, append the exception's partial stdout/stderr to the captured streams before returning operational_failure.
evidence: src/rebar/_bridge_runner.py:214: `    except subprocess.TimeoutExpired:`
src/rebar/_bridge_runner.py:215: `        stderr += f"Reconcile failed: timed out after {TIMEOUT_SECONDS} seconds\n"`
subprocess.TimeoutExpired carries partial .stdout/.stderr when capture_output=True; these are never appended to the returned result.
advisory.finding: On subprocess TimeoutExpired for both the reconcile and delivery subprocesses, any partial captured output on the exception (exc.stdout / exc.stderr) is discarded — only a synthesized 'timed out after N seconds' line is returned, so operator diagnostics from a slow/hung reconcile are lost.
scenarios: A reconcile pass emits useful progress then hangs and is killed at 3600s; the returned BridgeRun stderr contains only the generic timeout line.

dropped.finding: The MCP bridge_run tool declares default profile='dry-run', but run_bridge/_validate_environment unconditionally requires the full scheduled-delivery identity (BRIDGE_RUN_ID, BRIDGE_BOT_NAME, BRIDGE_BOT_EMAIL, JIRA_*, REBAR_ENV_ID) before any work, so a default dry-run invoked via MCP outside a CI-configured environment always returns state=invalid_invocation / returncode 2 rather than performing a preview.
